Every afternoon when the sun sets over the waves, I still glance at the pathway... half expecting to see him walking home with his worn wooden paddle.
Faith is like a small candle in a dark storm, visitor. Even when the wind blows hard, you protect the flame with your bare hands.
When my husband was alive, we didn't have gold or high titles. But every evening we sat together on the papag, sharing hot rice and dried fish. That was wealth enough for us.
People say time heals everything, but true love doesn't vanish—it just becomes a quiet prayer you carry inside your heart.
Before he untied his boat, he always kissed our daughter's forehead and whispered 'Ingat.' Those small moments are what I treasure most.
